title: Northforge Systems - Renewal & Regional Capacity Check-in
summary: Customer requested a 12-month extension with a staged capacity uplift (approx +50% tokens/month, EU region initial, APAC follow-on). Security and procurement need SOC2 evidence, SAML SSO integration notes, and KMS key flow. Redwood to send updated quote, security pack, and schedule a dedicated benchmark run with SE. Action items assigned and go/no-go milestone aligned for 2026-09-10.
action_items: Maya Patel: Deliver updated contract amendment & pricing with 50% uplift and EU add-on - due 2026-09-03
Ethan Cole: Run isolated benchmark (latency/throughput) using Northforge prompt set, record p95/p99 and sample traces - due 2026-09-07
Markus Vogel: Provide current traffic profile (seq length distribution, peak RPS windows, token/month) to Redwood - due 2026-08-31
Priya Singh: Confirm procurement timeline and required PO terms; identify internal legal reviewer - due 2026-09-01
next_steps: Send pricing amendment and one-page renewal summary
Share security package (SOC2 report, architecture diagram, SSO/KMS integration notes)
Schedule benchmark/SE-led deep dive w/ Northforge test prompts
Target decision checkpoint on or before 2026-09-10
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time, um, we've got about 40 minutes, so we'll cover renewal ask, the region onboarding, and next steps. Ethan's on for the technical bits.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Thanks Maya. Quick context — we've had Redwood in prod for 15 months, and it's been good. We're hitting sustained growth; tokens per month are up about 45% Q/Q, and we need to lock a renewal and add EU for latency. Markus and I will drive infra.
[00:27] Markus Vogel: morning, yeah sorry small delay, quick note — our current RPS profile: 120 peak, avg 35, sequence length median ~220 tokens, tail to 1.2k on search queries. We're on Hosted now but want EU region and scoped Dedicated vCPU/GPU pools later.
[00:44] Ethan Cole: Cool, thanks. How are you seeing latency targets? Are you p50/p95 set today?
[00:49] Lena Ortiz: p50 is fine, about 95ms on smaller prompts; p95 spikes to 1.1s during peaks. For EU customers we want p95 < 350ms ideally.
[00:58] Maya Patel: Ok that helps. So the ask in your email was a 12-month extension with an immediate +50% capacity uplift and EU region enabled, and APAC as a follow-on in Q1 next year, correct?
[01:10] Priya Singh: yes that is right. Also procurement asked about SOC2 and SSO — we need to validate compliance before we can sign.
[01:16] Maya Patel: understood. We'll include SOC2 attestations, SAML SSO docs, and KMS/HSM integration notes. We'll also add the audit log retention info you asked for.
[01:25] Markus Vogel: on Dedicated vs Hosted — right now we like Hosted but are evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput. There's a cost tradeoff; curious on Redwood's recommended runway before committing to Dedicated.
[01:36] Ethan Cole: Good question. Typical pattern we've seen: start with Hosted + region enablement and a moderate commit; run benchmark traces and if p95 or throughput or cost per token drives the need, then transition to Dedicated. Dedicated gives you fixed pool behaviour and lower variability for cold-starts, plus VPC options. But it does require a 3–6 week provisioning lead for reserved GPUs.
[01:54] Lena Ortiz: provisioning lead — that's fine, but timeline matters. We want EU enabled in 3 weeks. Is that realistic?
[02:00] Maya Patel: For Hosted EU region we can flip on within 7–10 business days, depending on capacity. For Dedicated EU pool, it's more like 3–5 weeks to provision nodes and verify SLOs. We can provide a staged plan: Hosted EU first, then a Dedicated migration window if you choose commits.
[02:14] Markus Vogel: Another thing — prefix/KV cache behavior with our RAG workloads. The docs mention KV caching but we saw inconsistent behavior on longer conversations, sometimes re-computing. Any known issues?
[02:27] Ethan Cole: The runtime uses KV caching but there are caveats with session pinning and varying sequence lengths. Also, transcription note: our docs sometimes say 'KV cache' but speech transcriber shows 'kay vee.' For you, we can instrument traces to show cache hit rates — that will help decide cache TTLs and batching.
[02:43] Lena Ortiz: perfect, we want the hit-rate and the effect on token cost. Cost/latency tradeoff is central.
[02:48] Priya Singh: On the procurement side, what about data residency? For EU, do we get guarantees that data stays within region? We need to confirm for our legal team.
[02:56] Maya Patel: For Hosted EU we support data locality and can enable region affinity; for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) you have full control. We'll include a data residency SLA statement in the security pack.
[03:08] Markus Vogel: encryption — KMS integration: we want customer-managed keys for embeddings and logs. Is HSM supported?
[03:15] Ethan Cole: Yes, we integrate with external KMS and can support HSM-backed key stores depending on deployment mode. For Hosted we support BYOK via supported cloud KMS providers; for Private you can leverage on-prem HSM. We'll include our KMS integration guide.
[03:27] Lena Ortiz: What about audit logs and retention? Also token-level cost visibility?
[03:31] Maya Patel: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and long-form audit logs as an add-on. We'll list retention tiers and pricing in the security appendix.
[03:40] Markus Vogel: about SLA — we need 99.9% uptime and a p95 latency commitment for the EU region. Can Redwood put that in the contract?
[03:49] Maya Patel: Our standard SLA for Dedicated supports 99.95% and we can commit to region-specific SLOs for Dedicated customers. For Hosted we have different tiers; we can propose a contract amendment with region-enabled SLOs for the EU add-on. I'll draft language for the 12-month amendment.
[04:05] Priya Singh: Are there penalty/credits for missing p95?
[04:08] Ethan Cole: Yes, we typically offer service credits scaled by severity. We'll provide the exact matrix in the amendment.
[04:13] Lena Ortiz: On pricing — high level: will the +50% uplift be a simple multiplier on our current committed tokens, or is there a new band? We want predictability.
[04:22] Maya Patel: We usually do tiered bands. For the uplift we can create a new committed band with predictable unit pricing and an overage rate. I'll put two options in the quote: a staged uplift (50% now, review at 6 months) and a flat uplift for full 12-months, with Dedicated commitment pricing as an alternative.
[04:38] Markus Vogel: Any discount for multi-region (EU + APAC) commit?
[04:42] Maya Patel: Yes, multi-region commits can be packaged for a volume discount. We'll show scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[04:48] Lena Ortiz: Regarding benchmarks — we need to run our prompt set to validate p95 numbers. Can Redwood run a full-run using our prompts? We prefer a blackbox run but with traces for cache/tokens.
[04:58] Ethan Cole: Absolutely. If Markus shares the prompt set and traffic profile, we can run a controlled benchmark in Hosted EU, include cold/warm cache runs, and provide p50/p95/p99 plus KV cache hit rates and per-token cost estimate. We'll schedule for next week.
[05:12] Markus Vogel: I'll anonymize the prompts and upload to the secure bucket. Also, for the KV cache tests please simulate our conversational flows where context grows to 2–4k tokens.
[05:21] Ethan Cole: noted — that will exercise the caching and quantization paths. We'll also test with quantized model variants to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:28] Lena Ortiz: On the legal front — Priya, timeline?
[05:31] Priya Singh: We're aiming to complete procurement approval within two weeks, but we need the SOC2 and sample contract language today. Also need to know payment terms and PO requirements.
[05:41] Maya Patel: We'll attach SOC2 and sample contract today, and include payment/PO language in the quote.
[05:44] Markus Vogel: One more technical — model variants and fallback. If EU capacity is saturated, can requests fall back to other regions without violating residency?
[05:53] Ethan Cole: There are two routing modes: strict region-only (no cross-region fallback) and latency-first with consent. For residency we can enable strict routing; for resilience, we can configure canary fallback to compatible model variants within EU or to Dedicated pools. We'll document routing policies and how to set policies per-route.
[06:10] Lena Ortiz: Ok. Also worried about botched transcriptions in earlier calls where model names got mislabelled; just flagging we need accuracy in reports.
[06:16] Maya Patel: Understood — we'll make sure pipeline artifacts label models consistently and include model-id mapping table.
[06:21] Priya Singh: Any competitors that offer lower price for EU-only?
[06:25] Lena Ortiz: we had CloudServe AI in early talks; their EU offering was cheaper but their performance wasn't great during our eval. OpenEndpoint popped up too.
[06:33] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll include a cost/perf comparison for the uplift scenarios.
[06:36] Markus Vogel: For the benchmark, can we also capture tail latencies for long seqs (2–4k)? That's where our p99 matters.
[06:43] Ethan Cole: yes, p99 will be included. We'll also include memory/kv cache pressure metrics and any eviction stats.
[06:49] Lena Ortiz: Great. Recap: Redwood to send updated contract & price, security pack, schedule benchmark; Northforge to provide prompt set and traffic profiles; decision checkpoint 2026-09-10. Anything else?
[07:02] Maya Patel: That covers it. I'll say one more thing — we'll propose a pilot run with a small Dedicated burst window as an optional add-on so you can observe Dedicated behavior without a full long-term commit.
[07:13] Markus Vogel: That might help sell internally.
[07:16] Priya Singh: Yes show us the numbers.
[07:18] Maya Patel: Perfect. We'll follow up via email tomorrow with the attachments and proposed dates. Thanks everyone.
[07:24] Lena Ortiz: thanks all.
[07:26] [END]
file_notes: Transcript contains typical transcription noise: proper nouns sometimes misrendered; timestamps are approximate. Speakers labeled by name when known; some overlap and brief crosstalk present.
